content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"Yes: the judge text decides the Acts 2:30 chain collision by treating the absence of an explicit naming of the body-channel as dispositive, which is the stating-verse approach the rule governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"none","why":"The judge leaves the collision open because no text explicitly names the body-channel, which is the retired stating-verse test rather than chain-against-chain footing."}
